questions.q: In the same vein as ‘Small Is Beautiful’, which expression does Maulana offer in this article?
options: ‘Bigger is Better’
The article mentions this phrase only as the contrast to Schumacher’s title.
‘Different is Beautiful’
This is the expression he offers, with differences of opinion in mind.
‘Silence is Golden’
This saying does not appear in the article.
‘Simple is Beautiful’
Close, but the article’s own expression is about difference.
questions.rationale: Differences of opinion should be used as a stepping stone rather than treated as an obstacle; a triggered mind becomes creative and discovers new facts and ideas.

questions.article: The Arabs and the Emergence of Islam
questions.q: Why does the article say that Arabia occupies a unique position?
options: It is the largest island in the world
The article calls it the largest peninsula, not an island.
It has the highest mountains in Asia
Mountains are not the reason given in the article.
It lies at the centre of three continents
Situated in Asia, it is divided from Africa only by the Red Sea and is a short passage from Europe.
It has the longest rivers in the world
The Euphrates and Tigris are mentioned only as part of its boundaries.
questions.rationale: With the Red Sea to the west and the Mediterranean within reach through the Suez canal, Arabia stands at the meeting point of Asia, Africa and Europe.

questions.article: Does the World of the Hereafter Exist?
questions.q: What did Sir James Jeans observe about the Creator of the universe?
options: That He must have possessed a mathematical mind
This is the observation quoted at the start of the article.
That He must have created the universe by chance
The article argues the opposite: the universe is meaningful and purposeful.
That He cannot be known through reason
The article applies scientific reasoning to the question.
That He created only the visible world
The article argues for the world of the Hereafter as well.
questions.rationale: The article adds that the meaningfulness of the universe shows that its Creator also had a deep sense of purpose, which points towards the Hereafter.

questions.q: What is spirituality called in Islam, according to this article?
options: Sawm
Sawm is fasting; it is not the word used here for spirituality.
Hijrah
Hijrah means migration and is not mentioned in this context.
Zakat
Zakat is almsgiving, not the term the article uses.
Rabbaniyat
It means turning one’s materialistic thinking into spiritual thinking.
questions.rationale: Health means a sound body, spirituality purifies the soul and develops the personality, and peace is essential for a healthy society. The three are linked to one another.

questions.q: According to the article, how can terrorism truly be brought to an end?
options: By stronger weapons alone
The article locates the root in ideology, which weapons cannot remove.
By countering the ideology of violence with an ideology based on peace
The article says terrorism will persist until this is done.
By ignoring it until it fades away
The article calls it one of the gravest threats, needing an intellectual response.
By isolating every religious community
The answer proposed is a positive presentation of Islam, not isolation.
questions.rationale: A person acts on a mission only when ideologically convinced. So the lasting answer is de-conditioning through the true and positive picture of Islam based on peace.

questions.q: What does the Quran call individuals who have undergone spiritual transformation?
options: “Ansar”
The Ansar were the Helpers of Madinah; that is not the term used here.
“Hanif”
This term appears in another article of this issue, not here.
“Rabbani”
Where such individuals exist in considerable numbers, a good society and state follow on their own.
“Muhajir”
This word is not used in the article.
questions.rationale: The individual is the real unit; society and the state are its relative parts. Reform therefore begins with the individual.

questions.q: What was Benjamin Franklin’s secret of success, in his own words?
options: “I will speak ill of no man, and speak all the good I know of everybody.”
These are the words quoted in the article.
“Early to bed and early to rise.”
A famous saying, but not the one quoted in this article.
“Honesty is the best policy.”
This is not the quotation given in the article.
“Time is money.”
This is not the quotation given in the article.
questions.rationale: The article then adds a caution: a man of principle upholds the truth, no matter what price has to be paid.

questions.q: When he was praised highly, how did Ibn Umar reply?
options: He thanked the man and asked him to say more
He did the opposite and warned that such praise can destroy a man.
He remained silent and walked away
The article records his spoken reply.
He said the praise was well deserved
He refused the praise altogether.
“I am just one of God’s servants; in Him do I have hope, and Him do I fear.”
He received praise with humility, not with conceit.
questions.rationale: The Companions’ lives are preserved as models. Ibn Umar’s answer shows how praise should be received: with humility and the remembrance of God.

questions.article: The Way of Balance and Moderation
questions.q: According to the article, where is balance and moderation required?
options: In religious beliefs, not in practical matters
It is the other way round.
In practical matters, not in religious beliefs or principles
In beliefs the ideal is always desirable; in practice, adjustment is wise.
In neither beliefs nor practice
The article affirms moderation in practical behaviour.
Only in matters of worship
The article speaks of practical life in society.
questions.rationale: Practical behaviour relates to external form and can be adjusted to prevailing conditions so that we live harmoniously with others.

questions.q: When his Companions asked him to curse his persecutors, what did the Prophet reply?
options: He asked them to leave the city at once
This is not the reply recorded in the article.
He told them to answer in the same manner
He taught the opposite: to return good for ill.
“I have not been sent to lay a curse upon men but to be a blessing to them.”
This is the reply reported in the books of Hadith.
He gave no answer
The article records his clear reply.
questions.rationale: The Quran introduces him as ‘a mercy to all mankind’ (21:107). His distinctive quality was being a blessing in word and deed.
